raw_case_text: In February 2001, a 39-year-old man was hospitalized in Marseilles, France, with fever and disorientation. This truck driver lived in Portugal and had been driving in Spain for 2 weeks before entering France. He arrived in France 3 days before admission. The day of admission, his co-workers found him confused and febrile after sleeping in his truck. He had no previous relevant medical history. On admission, his temperature was 40 C with tachycardia, and his blood pressure was 120/80 mm Hg. Clinical examination showed a drowsy, confused man with a bilateral headache, provoked myalgia of the legs, hepatalgia, and conjunctivitis. Neurologic examination showed signs of meningeal irritation, including cervical rigidity, Brudzinski's sign, hyperesthesia, and photophobia. There was no rash, and the rest of the physical examination was normal. Results of biochemical investigation included increased alanine aminotransferase (61 IU/L), aspartate aminotransferase (78 IU/L), lactate dehydrogenase (781 IU/L), fibrinogen level (6.44 g/L), and C-reactive protein (273 mg/L), associated with hypoglycemia (2.9 mmol/L), hypoalbuminemia (26 g/L), hypoproteinemia (54 g/L), and hypocholesterolemia (2.3 mmol/L). The leukocyte count was 11,000/mm3 with 69% polymorphonuclear forms. Thrombocytopenia (110 G/L) was also observed. The kaolin cephalin time was 58 s (control 34 s), and the prothrombin rate was 42%. Blood smears showed no parasites. Cerebral scanning was normal. Analysis of the CSF on day 1 showed 4 leukocytes/mm3, 50,000 erythrocytes/mm3, and elevated protein levels (1.48 g/L). On day 2, another CSF analysis showed 75 leukocytes/mm3, with 70% polymorphonuclear forms, 5,500 erythrocytes/mm3, and increased protein (0.64 g/L). Direct examination by dark-field microscopy of the CSF from day 2 was performed and controlled by two experimental investigators, who observed many spirochetes. The patient received a 10-day treatment with 12 g/day intravenous amoxicillin. The fever decreased to 38 C on day 4 and resolved on day 7. The patient was discharged from the hospital and remained well. No occupational or recreational risks for leptospirosis could be established. The patient had been traveling recently in Spain and Portugal but had no apparent exposure to sources of leptospires.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 39-year-old male truck driver presented with acute high fever and disorientation.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In February 2001, the patient was found confused and febrile by coworkers after sleeping in his truck in Marseilles, France, 3 days after arriving from a 2-week driving trip through Spain.
subjective.past_medical_history: No relevant past medical history. Resided in Portugal and worked as a long-distance truck driver in Spain and France; no specific occupational or recreational exposure to rodents or contaminated water was identified.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, confusion, bilateral headache, leg myalgia, and photophobia.

objective.physical_examination: On admission, temperature was 40 °C with tachycardia and blood pressure 120/80 mmHg. He was drowsy and confused with bilateral headache, provoked lower limb myalgia, hepatic tenderness (hepatalgia), and bilateral conjunctivitis, without cutaneous rash. Neurological exam revealed meningeal irritation including cervical rigidity, positive Brudzinski sign, hyperesthesia, and photophobia.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs: WBC 11,000/mm³ (69% polymorphonuclear cells), platelets 110 G/L, ALT 61 IU/L, AST 78 IU/L, LDH 781 IU/L, fibrinogen 6.44 g/L, CRP 273 mg/L, blood glucose 2.9 mmol/L, albumin 26 g/L, total protein 54 g/L, cholesterol 2.3 mmol/L, kaolin-cephalin clotting time 58 s (control 34 s), and prothrombin rate 42%. Peripheral blood smears were negative for parasites.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain CT scan was normal. Lumbar puncture CSF analysis on day 1 showed 4 leukocytes/mm³, 50,000 erythrocytes/mm³, and protein 1.48 g/L; repeat CSF on day 2 showed 75 leukocytes/mm³ (70% polymorphonuclear cells), 5,500 erythrocytes/mm³, and protein 0.64 g/L. Direct dark-field microscopy of day 2 CSF (independently verified by two investigators) demonstrated numerous motile spirochetes.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed acute neuroleptospirosis (leptospiral meningitis) with mild hepatic and coagulation involvement, diagnosed by direct visualization of spirochetes on dark-field microscopy of cerebrospinal fluid. Treated with IV amoxicillin 12 g/day for 10 days; fever decreased to 38 °C on day 4, resolved completely by day 7, and the patient was discharged home in good health.
